subject: POC scope: sample workload acceptance & cost guardrails
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@cloudline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: POC scope: sample workload acceptance & cost guardrails

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a concrete set of next steps so we can get the POC scheduled next week. I captured the evaluation focus you asked for and proposed measurement gates below. Please confirm or flag anything I missed.

Summary of what Cloudline will evaluate during the 2-week POC:
- Workload: 3 representative pipelines (Search rerank, Summarization for support tickets, Real-time chat assist). See attached sample_workload_spec.json for exact inputs.
- Traffic profile: peak concurrency ~80 qps, median 18 qps, request size distribution in the spec.
- Quality targets: rerank NDCG@10 >= 0.43 vs baseline, abstractive summarization ROUGE-L >= 0.62 (approx), chat response relevance score >= 4/5 from 20 sampled prompts.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile tail <= 600ms for chat (50-200 tokens), 95th <= 1.2s for rerank calls.
- Throughput target: sustained 1.2k tokens/sec per model variant during load test.
- Cost guardrail: target cost/token <= $0.0009 for the profile; fail if steady-state cost/token > $0.0012.

Deliverables we (Redwood) will provide before kickoff:
- Lightweight runbook and test harness (attached: cloudline_poc_requirements.xlsx).
- Pre-provisioned dedicated dev pool for the test window.
- Baseline model variant suggestions + quantization profile and estimated cost model (rdw-cost-model-v1.pdf).

Ownership and timeline:
- Cloudline to: provide sample payloads and 20 gold prompts for quality checks (Aisha, by EOD Thu 12/3).
- Redwood to: provision pool + upload harness and run initial smoke tests (Ben, by Mon 12/7).
- Joint: kickoff run on Tue 12/8 (tentative), two-week window with a mid-point sync and final review.

Immediate asks (please reply inline):
1) Confirm the three pipelines above align with what you expect to test.
2) Confirm Aisha can share the 20 gold prompts and a representative data slice by Thu 12/3.
3) Any legal or security hold-ups we should preempt (e.g., additional DPA terms)?

Thanks — I’ll schedule the kickoff invite once we lock dates.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Olga — this is great and very clear. Confirming the three pipelines are spot on. A couple of clarifications: 

- For the rerank pipeline, our baseline NDCG number is 0.40 (so your target is +0.03 uplift — sounds reasonable).
- For cost, we typically budget $30k for short pilots; your cost/token must map to an estimate we can include in the internal spend doc. Can you provide a short cost estimate by Friday?
- Security: we may need a short addendum for our procurement team that clarifies data retention for KV caches and whether logs are stored in the control plane. If you can have a one-pager, that would help accelerate procurement.

We’ll share the 20 gold prompts and a small data slice by EOD Thu 12/3. Also looping in our infra contact who will be on the kickoff call: Marco Rossi <marco.rossi@cloudline.ai>.

Appreciate it — excited to move forward.

Best,
Aisha Malik
Head of ML Ops | Cloudline Inc

Olga / Marcus — quick internal note and tech ask for the kickoff planning: 

1) Workload ingestion: we should ask Cloudline to provide payloads in newline-delimited JSON and include tokenized lengths distribution so we can precompute batching profiles. This helps us set the KV cache sizing and batching windows.
2) Latency measurement: prefer we instrument both client-side and server-side traces. Ben will add an extra tracing hook and a per-request token counter to the harness.
3) Cost-model tweak: rdw-cost-model-v1 assumes 8-bit quant and steady batching; if Cloudline cannot accept 8-bit we should prepare a 16-bit fallback with explicit delta. I can prepare two short cost scenarios (8-bit vs 16-bit) for Friday.

Ownership: Ben -> provisioning + harness changes; Marcus -> perf test scripts and SLO dashboards.

Also: attach a short checklist to the kickoff invite (smoke test steps, data redaction note).
